::: {.lead}
Today you work like in a lab: you give four jobs to an AI assistant, you
put the results into Word, and you check every answer. Do each experiment
when your teacher shows it. After each step, write your result in its box.
At the end, copy your key results into the table.
:::

## Before you start

- **You need:** a computer with Word, and an AI assistant that the
  university allows (for example Microsoft Copilot with your university
  account, at `copilot.microsoft.com`). Copilot inside Word is not needed.
- **Time:** about 40 minutes for the four experiments.
- **Check:** the results are at the end of this worksheet. On the
  interactive lesson, every step has "Check your result". Look only after
  you try.
- **Your words differ:** the AI writes a new text for every person. Check
  your answer with the facts, not with the words of the results.

{{< start-files >}}

## Experiment 1 · A first draft

**Aim:** let the AI write a first draft, then keep only your facts.
*(Lesson notes 5.1 · about 10 minutes)*

1. In the AI assistant, type this prompt: *Write a short notice for the
   staff of a small office. The printer on the first floor is broken.
   Please use the printer on the second floor until Tuesday. Three short
   lines.*

   {{< record "The first line of the draft" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   A good draft has your three facts: the printer on the **first floor** is
   broken, use the printer on the **second floor**, until **Tuesday**. The
   words differ for every person.
   :::

2. Read every line. Find every fact that you did **not** give, and delete
   it.

   {{< record "Facts that I did not give (or: none)" lines=2 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   The AI often adds something, for example "A technician comes on Monday"
   or "Call IT on 123". Nobody said it, so you delete it. If every fact is
   yours, write *none*. The draft keeps only your facts.
   :::

3. Copy the draft. Open a new Word document and paste with **Keep Text
   Only** (right-click › Paste Options › the button with the letter A).
   Give the first line the style **Title**, and save the file as
   `printer-notice.docx`.

   {{< record "Why Keep Text Only?" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **Keep Text Only** pastes only the words, without the look of the chat.
   Then the styles of Word give the look: the first line is a Title.
   :::

## Experiment 2 · A summary

**Aim:** let the AI sum up a report, and check every point with the
report. *(Lesson notes 5.2 · about 10 minutes)*

1. Open `report-start.docx` (click **Enable Editing** if you see it). Press
   **Ctrl + A** and **Ctrl + C**. In the AI assistant, type *Sum up this
   report in 3 short points:* and paste the report.

   {{< record "The 3 points, in a few words" lines=2 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   A good summary has three main points, for example: the second shop opens
   in Zarqa next Saturday at 9:00; it is open Saturday to Thursday, 9:00 to
   20:00; the first 50 customers get a free bag.
   :::

2. Compare each point with the report. Find every day, time, number and
   name in the report. Which details did the summary drop?

   {{< record "Right or changed? Dropped details:" lines=2 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   The points are usually right, but check each one: **Saturday**, **9:00**,
   **Zarqa**, **50** customers. A summary always drops details, for example
   the free pen for children or that the shop is closed on Friday. If a
   dropped detail matters to your reader, add it again.
   :::

3. Open **Word AI Lab** on the interactive lesson and choose **Sum up**.
   Compare the three points with the memo and tap the wrong part.

   {{< record "The wrong part, and the right fact" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   "Shop staff pick up the price list at **3 pm**": the memo says **5 pm**.
   A summary can change a number, so you find it in the original.
   :::

## Experiment 3 · A new tone

**Aim:** let the AI say the same facts in other words, and keep the facts.
*(Lesson notes 5.3 · about 10 minutes)*

1. In the AI assistant, type: *Rewrite this in a polite, formal tone for a
   customer: "We do not have your size. Come back next week."*

   {{< record "The new sentence" lines=2 >}}

   ::: {.check}
   A good rewrite: "Dear customer, we are sorry, but your size is not in
   the shop now. Please visit us again next week." The facts stay: no size
   now, come back next week.
   :::

2. Check the rewrite. Did the AI add a promise or a new fact, for example a
   discount, a call or a date?

   {{< record "Added: … (or: nothing)" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   If the AI added "We will call you" or "You get a 10 % discount", delete
   it: the shop did not promise it. A rewrite changes the words and the
   tone, never the facts.
   :::

3. Do the three tasks of **Tone Lab** on the interactive lesson.

   {{< record "Task 1 … ; Task 2 … ; Task 3 …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **Task 1:** formal and short (a customer that you have never met).
   **Task 2:** friendly and short (a customer who is your friend).
   **Task 3:** formal and long (a letter for the company file).
   :::

## Experiment 4 · A translation

**Aim:** translate in Word, then check the days, times, numbers and names.
*(Lesson notes 5.4 · about 10 minutes)*

1. In `report-start.docx`, select the second paragraph (*Sunrise Company
   opens its second shop …*). Choose **Review › Translate › Translate
   Selection** and the language **Arabic**.

   {{< record "The day and the time in Arabic" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   A right translation says **السبت** (Saturday) and **9:00** (الساعة
   التاسعة), and the names **الزرقاء** and **شارع الملك عبدالله**. No
   Translate in your Word? Use Word on the web.
   :::

2. Now select the paragraph with the first day (*On the first day, the
   first 50 customers …*) and translate it. Check the numbers.

   {{< record "50 and 12 in the translation: right or wrong?" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   The translation must keep **50** customers (٥٠) and children under
   **12** (١٢). If a number, a day or a name is different, correct it before
   you use the text.
   :::

3. In **Word AI Lab**, choose **Translate**. Compare the Arabic with the
   English memo and tap the wrong part.

   {{< record "The wrong word, and the right one" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **الثلاثاء** is Tuesday, but the memo says Thursday: **الخميس**. A
   machine translation can change a day, so you check it.
   :::
